messages:
julia: CI microbench failure on PR #5190 — batch scheduler perf regressed for small seqs (<64). Artifact: https://ci.internal.redwood/arti/5190/batch_scheduler_smallseq
julia: Repro (locally): ./scripts/run_perf.sh --bench batch_scheduler --runs 100 --seq 32
ci-bot: Perf check: threshold exceeded for batch_scheduler_smallseq: -18.4% (baseline 12.4ms -> 14.7ms). Compare: https://ci.internal.redwood/artifacts/5190/summary.html
matt: thanks — looking now, will try a local bisect.
matt: quick update: bisected between main@abc123 (good) and merge@def456 (bad). The merge includes commits touching kernel selector and batching heuristics. Early suspicion: kernel selector change that prefers small-seq kernels by default.
matt: repro logs (trimmed):
```
commit def456: batch_scheduler: +prefers_small_seq_kernels=true
run: 100 iters seq=32: avg 14.7ms
commit abc123: prefers_small_seq_kernels=false
run: 100 iters seq=32: avg 12.3ms
```
sanjay: hmm that flag was intended to help long sequences get better kernel layouts, but seems to regress small-seq perf. It might change kernel selection ordering causing suboptimal CUDA kernel until cache warms.
olivia: can you upload a flamegraph / nvprof capture for both commits? Also curious about KV cache hit-rate — small seq workloads rely on prefix caching a lot.
matt: uploaded profiles: https://perf.internal.redwood/5190/def456/flame.svg and https://perf.internal.redwood/5190/abc123/flame.svg
matt: nvprof shows a longer memcpy path and increased kernel launch count on def456.
sanjay: I pulled KV stats from the run — hit rate dropped by ~4.7% on def456 for these workloads. That could increase effective token work and amplify kernel cost.
kevin: putting canary rollout on hold until this is fixed :no_entry_sign:
julia: agreed — please do not merge release candidate while this is active.
matt: quick fix test: reverted the prefers_small_seq_kernels change locally -> small seq perf returns to baseline. Long sequence perf decreases slightly but within acceptable delta.
sanjay: proposal: gate the new kernel preference behind an adaptive heuristic that looks at recent seq distribution and KV hit-rate. If small-seq-heavy, keep old kernels.
olivia: also suggest adding a microbench perf unit that covers seq 8/16/32 with cold/warm cache permutations so CI flags regressions earlier.
julia: action items:
- matt to open a revert PR for the selector flag (PR 5192) and add the small-seq microbench test
- sanjay to prototype adaptive heuristic and KV-aware toggle
- olivia to add perf artifacts and link them in PR
- kevin to keep canary hold until revert is merged and perf green
matt: opened revert PR 5192 -> https://git.internal.redwood/pr/5192
ci-bot: Perf CI triggered for PR 5192: https://ci.internal.redwood/5192/perf (waiting)
kevin: thanks, team. once the revert passes perf CI we'll iterate on a safer rollout for the kernel selector change.
julia: thanks all — keep updates here. If someone fixes this in a non-revert way, please post the perf numbers for both small and long seqs so we can re-evaluate the rollout.
